study.title: Immediate neural effects of acupuncture manipulation time for stroke with motor dysfunction: a fMRI pilot study
study.study_design: Pilot study, randomized, three-group parallel design
study.randomization: Central randomization system; based on a special six-digit random number that was automatically produced by the system
study.blinding: Outcome measurement completed by an independent evaluator who did not know what manipulation each participant received; group assignment concealed from participants
study.inclusion_criteria: (1) ischemic stroke diagnoses according to the International Classification of Diseases, 10th reversion (ICD-10-I63.902); (2) motor dysfunction; (3) first onset and the disease course less than 3 months; and (4) age between 40 and 80 years old, right-handed
study.exclusion_criteria: (1) had participated in other clinical trials within the last 2 weeks; (2) had serious underlying diseases or complications; (3) women who were pregnant, menstruating, lactating; and (4) had contraindications of MRI scan

interventions.manipulation_exact: The acupuncturist held the needle handle with the thumb and forefinger and rotated the needle body in an alternating clockwise and counterclockwise manner, the twist frequency was 120 times per minute and the angle was about 180°. Three acupoints were manipulated one by one in sequence after the needle produced the Deqi sensation. Each acupoint received continuous manipulation for 1-min. The needles had been pulled out immediately after the manipulation was completed.
interventions.deqi_intended_exact: Three acupoints were manipulated one by one in sequence after the needle produced the Deqi sensation (a soreness, numbness, and heaviness sensation)
interventions.needle_retention_exact: Needles pulled out immediately after manipulation was completed
interventions.session_duration_exact: Total manipulation time: 3 min (3 acupoints × 1 min each)
interventions.treatment_rationale_given_exact: Governor Meridian is closely connected to the brain in Chinese medical theory and is frequently employed in the treatment of neuropsychiatric diseases

extraction_notes.note: No adverse events section was included in the paper. Adverse events were not explicitly reported or stated to be absent.

Expectancy, credibility, and blinding success of participants were not assessed or reported in this study. The paper mentions participant blinding (group assignment concealed) and evaluator blinding but provides no quantitative measure.

Deqi sensation was described as a prerequisite for manipulation but was not formally quantified using any instrument (e.g., MASS, Southampton Needle Sensation Questionnaire). No quantitative deqi scores are reported.
Table 2 header uses 'NHISS' (appears to be a typo in the PDF for 'NIHSS'). Data extracted as NIHSS consistent with the rest of the text.

The T-value of -29.98 for the 1-min group inferior frontal gyrus (Table 3) is unusually large in magnitude for n=10. This may reflect the scale of the paired T-test output from DPABI software. Extracted as reported.

The direction of the between-group contrast is encoded in the condition label '2-min > 1-min', '3-min > 2-min', '3-min > 1-min' in Table 4 but the T-values are negative for some rows (precentral gyrus: -7.77; posterior cingulate gyrus: -7.87; anterior cingulate gyrus: -8.31), indicating that the actual change is lower in the higher-dose group. Separate contrast entries were created for increased and decreased findings within the same arm comparison.

The paper states the fMRI-BOLD matrix was 64×64 with FOV=240mm×240mm and slice thickness=3mm, but does not explicitly state in-plane resolution or number of slices. Voxels were re-sampled to 3-mm3 during preprocessing.

No between-group comparison of NIHSS or FMA scores after treatment is explicitly reported with a test statistic or p-value in Table 2. Text states 'the NIHSS and FMA scores were not statistically significant between-group differences at baseline (p> 0.05)' but does not report post-treatment between-group statistics.
extraction_notes.source_location: Page 3-4, Results/Demographics and clinical information section; Page 4, Table 2

extraction_notes.note: The paper does not report needle type, gauge, or length used for acupuncture.
No sham or placebo control group was included in this study. All three arms received active acupuncture at the same acupoints with different manipulation durations.

The study does not report whether the 1-min group's inferior frontal gyrus decrease represents a statistically significant within-group change in the traditional sense (the T-value is negative and large). The paper reports this as an activation/change in the longitudinal within-group analysis.
extraction_notes.source_location: Page 4-5, Results/ReHo analysis results/Within-group section; Figure 1A; Table 3

extraction_notes.note: The session_duration_min_numeric for each arm was inferred by multiplying manipulation time per acupoint (1, 2, or 3 min) by number of acupoints (3). This is not explicitly stated as total session duration in the paper.

Conventional treatment details (physical rehabilitation, secondary prevention of cerebral infarction) were documented but not reported quantitatively in the paper. No analysis of conventional treatment differences between groups is provided.

Figure 1 and Figure 2 display brain activation maps. Coordinates for these figures are reported in Table 3 and Table 4 respectively. No additional coordinates appear to be shown exclusively in figures.
